title: Continuous sections of a topological module sequence with finite discrete quotient
statement:
Let $A,T_0,T_1,T_2$ be commutative topological rings, with continuous unital homomorphisms $A\to T_i$ giving their $A$-module structures. Let $f:T_0\to T_1$ and $g:T_1\to T_2$ be continuous $A$-linear maps. Suppose $f$ is injective, $g$ is surjective, $\operatorname{im}f=\ker g$, $T_2$ is finite and discrete, and the induced bijection $T_0\to\ker g$ is a homeomorphism for the subspace topology on $\ker g$. For every profinite set $S$, the sequence of pointwise $C(S,A)$-modules
$$0\to C(S,T_0)\xrightarrow{f\circ-}C(S,T_1)\xrightarrow{g\circ-}C(S,T_2)\to0$$
is short exact. The postcomposition maps consequently give a short exact sequence of condensed $\underline A$-module objects $0\to\underline{T_0}\to\underline{T_1}\to\underline{T_2}\to0$, using the continuous-function sheaves of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

source.place: On the point: continuous division through the topological kernel and lifting the finite discrete values; Triangles: the same argument for quotient powers. General topological-module formulation of that argument.

proof.text: Fix a profinite set $S$ and write $\alpha_i:A\to T_i$ for the scalar maps. The scalar action is continuous by continuity of the scalar maps and multiplication. Use the continuous-section module objects of [def-sfb-continuous-sections-module], whose sections have pointwise action $(a\cdot u)(s)=\alpha_i(a(s))u(s)$. Set $F_S(u)=f\circ u$ and $G_S(v)=g\circ v$. Continuity follows by composition. The pointwise equalities $f(u+v)=f(u)+f(v)$ and $f(\alpha_0(a)u)=\alpha_1(a)f(u)$, and the same equalities for $g$, make these maps $C(S,A)$-linear. The module axioms hold by evaluation, using the ring and algebra axioms.

source.place: On the point: the pointwise module sequence

proof.text: If $F_S(u)=F_S(v)$, then $f(u(s))=f(v(s))$ for every $s$, so injectivity of $f$ gives $u=v$. Moreover $g(f(t))=0$ for every $t\in T_0$, since $\operatorname{im}f=\ker g$. Hence $G_SF_S=0$ and $\operatorname{im}F_S\subseteq\ker G_S$.

source.place: On the point: injectivity and the zero composite

proof.text: Let $v\in C(S,T_1)$ satisfy $G_S(v)=0$. Its values lie in $K=\ker g$. The map $\bar v:S\to K$ with the same values is continuous for the subspace topology: the inverse image of $K\cap U$ is $v^{-1}(U)$ for every open $U\subseteq T_1$. By hypothesis $h:T_0\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, $t\mapsto f(t)$, is a homeomorphism. Therefore $u=h^{-1}\circ\bar v$ is continuous and $F_S(u)=v$. Combined with step 2, this proves $\operatorname{im}F_S=\ker G_S$.

source.place: On the point: continuous division through the topological kernel

proof.text: For each $b\in T_2$ choose $t_b\in T_1$ with $g(t_b)=b$, using surjectivity of $g$. Given $w\in C(S,T_2)$, define $v(s)=t_{w(s)}$. For an open $U\subseteq T_1$ one has $v^{-1}(U)=\bigcup_{b:t_b\in U}w^{-1}(\{b\})$, an open set since $T_2$ is discrete. Thus $v$ is continuous and $G_S(v)=w$. This proves surjectivity and completes the short exact sequence on sections. The choices $t_b$ need not define a linear map; only the lift of each individual section is required.

source.place: On the point: lifting the finitely many values of the quotient

proof.text: The maps $F_S,G_S$ commute with precomposition, hence give abelian-sheaf maps. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], the source of an action is the sheafification of the objectwise tensor presheaf. By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], maps to the target sheaf correspond uniquely to maps from that presheaf. Additive maps from a tensor product agree if they agree on pure tensors. On $a\otimes u$, action compatibility is $f(\alpha_0(a(s))u(s))=\alpha_1(a(s))f(u(s))$ at each $s$, and similarly for $g$. Thus [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] gives internal maps on [def-sfb-continuous-sections-module]. Their composite is zero by step 2, since underlying maps agree on all sections.

source.place: On the point: continuous division through the topological kernel and lifting the finite discrete values; Triangles: the same argument for quotient powers. General topological-module formulation of that argument.

proof.text: Take profinite sets in universe $u$ and coefficient groups in $u+1$, so the profinite site is essentially small relative to these groups. The underlying section groups of our internal modules are $C(S,T_i)$, with the same arrows as steps 1--4. Those steps verify every evaluated sequence is short exact. Apply [lem-pe-internal-module-sectionwise-short-exact] to the internal maps of step 5. It gives short exactness in condensed $\underline A$-modules with precisely the prescribed postcomposition arrows.
